summary: A club's wooden lookout from 1887 became a state fire tower; the 1930 steel tower is restored, open to the public, and has volunteer weekends.

facts.design: Steel frame tower with an enclosed cab, reached by seven flights of steel stairs

staffing.status: volunteers on some weekends in season

access.note: NHLR describes the tower as open to the public; the summit route is a former jeep road about 3 miles long from Mill Brook Road, now a hiking trail.

visit.trail_note: About 3 miles on the former summit jeep road from Mill Brook Road, now a hiking trail.

facts.agency: New York State Department of Environmental Conservation

events.note: Wooden tower put up by the Balsam Lake Club to guard its land against fire; state guide calls it the first forest fire tower in New York
Club tower struck by lightning and burned down about 1901 (NHLR); the state guide says it survived until 1901
Club built a similar wooden tower on the summit
Facility transferred to the state when its fire tower system began
Present 47-foot steel tower built (state guide); Wikipedia gives Built 1930
Added to the National Register of Historic Places September 23, 2001, reference 01001038

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The state guide gives the present tower as 47 feet tall; Wikipedia gives 47 1/2 feet (14.5 m). The story reports both and the record uses Wikipedia's 14.5 m.

notes_for_editor: Built dates agree across the three sources (1887 club tower, 1905 wooden replacement, 1919 first steel tower, 1930 present tower) once the NHLR, state guide and Wikipedia are read together. Wikipedia's section heading dates the club's establishment 1885-1909 but its text says 1887; the story uses 1887. Height differs (47 vs 47 1/2 ft). The reopening year is not stated in the Wikipedia text read, so no restoration year is recorded. The access and staffing evidence is from a 2017 NHLR visit report, so current status should be checked. The state guide is a multi-column PDF; its quotes were taken from single lines. Wikipedia's coordinates (42.06972, -74.57444) differ from the record's (42.045395, -74.594604), which matches NHLR; left unchanged. A later NHLR visit report says the tower is open Friday to Sunday, but it is undated in the text read, so it was not used.
